examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: A control store maps microinstruction addresses to control signals and next-address decisions. Horizontal encoding exposes many independent control bits; vertical encoding uses compact fields and decoding. Distinguish control-memory word width from address width. Branch conditions and instruction dispatch can make the microprogram nonsequential.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A control store has 512 microinstructions of 40 bits each. What is its capacity in bytes?

**Answer: 2560.** Capacity is 512·40=20480 bits, or 20480/8=2560 bytes. The microaddress requires 9 bits but is not multiplied into the control-word capacity unless explicitly stored as part of each word.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Microprogrammed control is not the same as user-program instructions in main memory. Writable control stores and ROM-based stores have different update possibilities.

A microinstruction is not the same as a programmer-visible machine instruction.
